title: Trigonometry: Law of Sines for AAS and ASA Practice
description: Practice solving AAS and ASA oblique triangles with the Law of Sines.

questions.question: Why are ordinary right-triangle ratios not enough for a general oblique triangle?
options: An oblique triangle has no guaranteed right angle or hypotenuse.
An oblique triangle always has three equal sides.
The angles of an oblique triangle do not add to 180°.
Sine cannot be used with oblique triangles.
questions.explanation: Right-triangle ratios are organized around a right angle and a hypotenuse. Oblique triangles need relationships such as the Law of Sines.

questions.question: Which formula shows the Law of Sines?
options: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
questions.explanation: The Law of Sines compares every side with the sine of its opposite angle.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 54°, ∠B = 64°, and a = 16. Which expression finds b?
questions.explanation: Use b/sin 64° = 16/sin 54°, so b = 16 sin 64° / sin 54°.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 52°, ∠B = 73°, and b = 24. What is a to the nearest tenth?
In △ABC, ∠A = 37°, ∠B = 69°, and a = 10. What are b and c to the nearest tenth?
In an ASA triangle, the known side is between the two known angles.
questions.explanation: ASA means angle-side-angle, so the given side is included between the two given angles.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 49°, ∠B = 58°, and a = 14. Find b to the nearest tenth.
In △ABC, ∠A = 71°, ∠C = 44°, and a = 21. Find b to the nearest tenth.
A student sets up a Law of Sines proportion as a/sin B = b/sin A. Explain the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: The student switched the opposite pairs. Side a must be paired with sin A, and side b must be paired with sin B.
questions.explanation: The Law of Sines works only when every side is matched with the sine of its opposite angle.
